Differences: Session charges one talk per checklist giver (Model one per stop), clamps a count at 0 (Model at 1), and returns nil for dungeon/battlemaster steps and explore slots (16) where Model estimates. The checklist and nil cases look intentional (a time budget must not guess); the 0-vs-1 clamp and the duplicated 7 yd/s and 4 s/10 s constants are accidental drift: a retune of the lap cost model silently leaves the session budget on the old numbers.

The copies differ in units, per-stop versus per-giver talk costs, minimum-one versus minimum-zero counts, missing-count defaults versus rejection, and explore/dungeon/battlemaster rejection; the finite-cost versus optional-duration contract forces divergence, and matching 7/4/10 constants alone does not establish accidental drift.

items.why: `rg -il roadmap` finds no roadmap document, only comments; docs/design.md:40 does carry '2.16 Professions', so the design reference alone is enough. The same label style appears in Core/State.lua, Core/Core.lua and types/Namespace.lua, so the owner may prefer one repo-wide decision.
items.reason: The lens excludes the project's established documentation convention: numbered roadmap references consistently connect runtime comments, specs and type contracts, including #9 in UI/Hints/Profession.lua, tests/profession_spec.lua and types/Namespace.lua on origin/cb/route-stop-api. The accompanying docs/design.md §2.16 resolves and agrees with Model.Profession, so the missing standalone roadmap does not establish drift from that convention.

items.quote: local instance = journey.kind == "dungeon" and tonumber(journey.key:match("^dungeon:(%d+)$"))
items.what: A journey's zone or instance ID is recovered by pattern-matching its key string at every read site instead of being a typed field Model sets once; add the ID to AGFJourney (or one Model accessor) and read that.
items.why: rg '\^zone:|\^dungeon:|\^chain:' finds the key encoding (written in Planning/Model.lua:3122, 3299, 3366, 3435) re-parsed with a literal pattern in UI/Menu.lua:104, UI/Overview.lua:362, UI/Moments.lua:64 and :67, Integrations/Providers.lua:89, UI/WindowGuide.lua:15, Core/Core.lua:129 and :622-623, and Planning/Model.lua:3675, 3825, 4061. The key is a persisted identity (prefs.journey), which is a wire format, but it is not converted once at a boundary: types/Namespace.lua AGFJourney has no zone or instance field, so each consumer carries its own copy of the pattern. A typo in one pattern, or a new key prefix, is not found by LuaLS or luacheck; the mismatch silently yields nil (no dungeon page entry, wrong moment text, zone left out of Completion).
items.reason: Applied on cb/sift-decisions.

items.quote:
local function ShowOnMap(step)
	FocusStep(step)
end
items.what: ShowOnMap forwards to FocusStep, which itself only forwards to ns.Pins.Reveal: two wrapper layers over one call; keep one name (export FocusStep's body as Overview.ShowOnMap and call it from RowClick) or call ns.Pins.Reveal directly.
items.why: UI/Overview.lua:25-27 FocusStep is `ns.Pins.Reveal(step)` and nothing else; 513-515 ShowOnMap is `FocusStep(step)` and nothing else. `rg 'ShowOnMap|FocusStep'` over the repo: FocusStep has two users (RowClick at Overview.lua:299 and ShowOnMap); Overview.ShowOnMap is called from UI/WindowGuide.lua:188 and UI/WindowJourneys.lua:94,303. Neither layer adds an argument, guard or return value, and no second implementation exists (Integrations.ShowOnMap is a different function with a different contract). Collapsed form: one `local function ShowOnMap(step) ns.Pins.Reveal(step) end` used by RowClick and exported.
items.guard: lens-only: needs to know the wrapper has one implementation and no second caller planned

items.quote:
Overview.HubLine = HubLine
Overview.DropLine = DropLine
Overview.Progress = Progress
items.what: Overview hands out the pieces of a card's third line and footer (DropLine, HubLine, Progress, Stops) and each caller reassembles them in the same order: UI/Panel.lua:792 and UI/WindowJourneys.lua:248 for a whole card, UI/Panel.lua:1054-1057 and UI/WindowJourneys.lua:269-273 for a compact or grid card.
items.why: rg 'DropLine\(|HubLine\(' returns the two pairs: `DropLine(journey) or journey.reason or HubLine(journey) or ""` verbatim in Panel.lua:792 and WindowJourneys.lua:248, and the four-step sequence `value, label = Progress(journey)`; `foot = label or Stops(journey)`; `reason = journey.reason ~= foot and journey.reason or nil`; `DropLine(journey) or reason or HubLine(journey) or journey.subline` in Panel.lua:1054-1057 and WindowJourneys.lua:269-273. CardTooltip (Overview.lua:394-400) then has to guess which of those lines the card showed (`card.detail == hub`, `card.state == "compact"`). The precedence rule (log-full note, then reason, then hub, then subline) is the thing Overview's header says panel and window must never disagree on, and it lives in the callers; the reason line and the footer/progress pair would move behind Overview.
items.reason: The shallow-modules exclusion for a caller needing the pieces apart applies: UI/WindowJourneys.lua:254-263 uses Progress independently for the featured footer, hiding it without progress, while grid cards fall back to Stops. Overview.CardTooltip also uses HubLine independently, so the exported pieces serve varying compositions despite the repeated detail precedence.

items.quote: and (provider and L.CLICK_TRAVEL:format(provider) or L.CLICK_WAYPOINT)
items.what: The aside's click dispatch and tooltip are written out in UI/Panel.lua:444-465 (CreateAsideLine) and again in UI/Window.lua:408-429 (CreateChip), with the click dispatch a third time in UI/Tracker.lua:80-86 and the click-line wording a third time in UI/Pins.lua:41-44 (AddClickLine); move one handler pair next to ns.Asides.Open/Go (UI/Asides.lua, or UI/Overview.lua which already holds what panel and window share) and have all three call it.
items.why: rg 'CLICK_TRAVEL|CLICK_WAYPOINT' returns UI/Panel.lua:462, UI/Window.lua:427 and UI/Pins.lua:43 with the same `provider and L.CLICK_TRAVEL:format(provider) or L.CLICK_WAYPOINT` expression; rg 'MENU_ADVENTURE_GUIDE_FOREVER_ASIDE' returns Panel.lua:447, Window.lua:412, Tracker.lua:82, each the same right-click Asides.Open / else Asides.Go branch. Panel.lua:453-465 and Window.lua:418-429 are token-identical (Window's comment says 'As the panel's aside line'). No difference between the copies is intentional: a change to the wanderer rule or the provider wording has to land in all of them.
